title: De-risk WKWebView video rendering continuously at desktop level on Tahoe
description: The ow-mbw.1 spike de-risks an AppKit + CoreAnimation desktop-level window, but the product render path (DEC-001) is a looping <video> inside a transparent WKWebView, which uses a different compositor path (IOSurface / render-server) that macOS has historically throttled independently. A green AppKit/CA spike does NOT prove the real wallpaper keeps animating. This task validates: a muted+playsinline looping <video> in a transparent WKWebView, pinned at CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopWindow), keeps decoding and compositing new frames continuously on macOS 26 (behind icons, click-through, all Spaces, and crucially after >=2 minutes with another app frontmost, i.e. not frozen by occlusion or App Nap). Reuse the validated window factory from ow-mbw.1.
design: Throwaway env-gated (OW_WEBSPIKE=1) WebKit de-risk, mutually exclusive with OW_SPIKE. NEW WebSpikeWindow.swift (only file allowed WKWebView): copies the measured ow-mbw.1 window property table (NOT makeSpikeWindow) with isOpaque=false + backgroundColor=.clear; WKWebViewConfiguration.mediaTypesRequiringUserActionForPlayback=[] (NOT allowsInlineMediaPlayback, iOS-only); transparency via underPageBackgroundColor=.clear + CSS (NO drawsBackground KVC, private); loadFileURL(allowingReadAccessTo:); telemetry via WKScriptMessageHandler; polls WKMediaPlaybackState; logs webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate; enumerates PID-owned on-screen windows and flags any layer >= desktop-icon level. Throwaway web/webspike/{index.html,style.css,app.js}: full-bleed muted playsinline loop autoplay video, no controls, disablepictureinpicture, disableremoteplayback, filter: brightness(1.01) (DEC-001 chose WKWebView FOR filters; a filter forces the freezable backing-store recomposite, so test WITH a filter). Oracle: machine-readable COLOR BLOCK driven by frame# burned into the VIDEO (not a JS HUD) in a known center-fraction crop; RVFC presented-frame counter; postMessage telemetry only. Asset: ffmpeg H.264 yuv420p 1920x1080@30, 17.3s (non-divisor of 120), -an (NO audio: a silent track can hold a media power assertion that masks App Nap), color-block + human digits, generated into .build/webspike/ (NOT in-tree).
acceptance_criteria: A transparent WKWebView desktop-layer window shows a continuously playing video behind icons that is still advancing after a >=2 minute occluded watch on AC power.
notes: PASS with benign occlusion nuance. The WKWebView <video> at the desktop layer keeps presenting frames continuously whenever its Space is visible: WebKit does NOT throttle the hidden/occluded page (RVFC presentedFrames advance with document.visibilityState=hidden, media=playing for 125s, no WebContent termination). Proven on glass by screencapture -l showing the burned-in counter advancing. Direct Phase 5 observation (Anoop): visible wallpaper animates (incl. behind a same-Space maximized window); a display taken into its own full-screen Space pauses (macOS occlusion/Space culling) and RESUMES live on return (not frozen). So screencapture -l of a 100%-occluded window is not a freeze oracle (it measures compositor culling); the authoritative liveness signals are RVFC + media=playing + a VISIBLE window animating, all of which passed. 4 cold Codex passes; final adjudication: transparency gating REJECTED (by design, a reported finding for ow-94b.1); z-order actual-layer assert + OW_WEBSPIKE_ACTIVITY env hygiene FIXED; per-window-telemetry-id, cmp-byte-diff, and foreground-app-assertion documented as known throwaway-check limitations (authoritative oracle is direct observation + per-window pixel gate + RVFC). Follow-ups: multi-display slice sync across pause/resume (ow-blz.5); true idle App Nap not exercised (ow-aad.1). Findings: ow-local/systems/web-render/webview-video-spike-findings.md.
close_reason: De-risk PASS: a looping, filtered, muted <video> in a transparent WKWebView at the desktop window level keeps presenting frames continuously on Tahoe whenever its Space is visible (WebKit does not throttle the occluded/hidden page; RVFC + media=playing sustained 125s; proven on glass). Fully-hidden windows pause via macOS occlusion culling and resume live (benign). Validated by direct observation + automated gates. Seeds ow-94b.1. Follow-ups: ow-blz.5 (slice sync), ow-aad.1 (idle App Nap).

title: web/ files: looping video page (index.html, style.css, wallpaper.js)
description: index.html with <video> (muted, playsinline, loop) + overlay canvas; style.css full-bleed object-fit cover; wallpaper.js autoplay kick on canplay. Black fallback until video loads.
design: Port the VALIDATED webspike page (not a new recipe). web/index.html: full DOCTYPE+head with <link rel=stylesheet href=style.css>, <meta charset>; body has #stage > <video id=bg muted playsinline autoplay loop preload=auto disablepictureinpicture disableremoteplayback aria-hidden tabindex=-1><source src=assets/bg.mp4 type=video/mp4></video> + <canvas id=overlay aria-hidden>; <script src=wallpaper.js>. web/style.css: html{color-scheme:only light}; html,body,#stage full-size margin0 overflow hidden background:#000 (opaque base + black fallback); #bg + #overlay absolute inset:0 100%x100%; #bg object-fit:cover object-position:center AND filter: brightness(1.01) (KEEP: the validated recomposite path from 94b.5, DEC-001); NO opacity:0/.video-ready gate (video opacity 1; black CSS is the fallback, first frame covers it); #overlay z-index above video, pointer-events none, CSS-ONLY (no JS backing-store sizing: Epic D owns it). web/wallpaper.js: autoplay-ONLY IIFE: tryPlay() sets muted/defaultMuted/playsInline true then video.play().catch(); bind canplay+loadeddata; AND call tryPlay() IMMEDIATELY (synchronous kick, the spike pattern: local file+preload can reach canplay before a deferred script); add ended->tryPlay() belt; NO canvas JS, NO visibilitychange retry. WebWallpaperView.swift: ADD a native playback signal (no script handler): in didFinish (and a 1s follow-up) call self.requestMediaPlaybackState and log 'ONLYWALLPAPERS_WEB screen=<name> win=<n> media=playing|paused|none|suspended'. scripts/generate-test-bg.sh (COMMITTED): generate a moving, high-contrast, counter-burned, yuv420p+faststart, -an H.264 clip (~5-8s) into web/assets/bg.mp4 (gitignored); pin a system fontfile for drawtext or use drawbox for motion; reuse the spike's proven vf graph. scripts/video-check.sh (production liveness gate): generate the asset, launch the DEFAULT app, wait for loaded=ok, assert native media=playing per win, screencapture -l A/B ~0.5s apart (band-diff differ) + C at >clip-duration (counter wrapped), fail-closed/INCONCLUSIVE on -l TCC fail. smoke-run.sh: add SHAPE greps on index.html/style.css/wallpaper.js (muted, loop, playsinline, src=assets/bg.mp4, object-fit, video.play, <canvas, filter) as shape guards only (label as such); smoke stays TCC-free (playback gate is video-check.sh). Do NOT retire the webspike in this task (keep the A/B; retirement deferred). Boundaries: no Package.swift/Bundle.module (94b.3), no committed real video (94b.4), no moods/config (Epic D), no slice geometry (ow-blz.2). Update web-render/overview.md (wallpaper.js is autoplay-only now; slice transform planned ow-blz.2).
acceptance_criteria: A looping video fills the wallpaper window and starts on its own.
notes: ADJUDICATION (final Codex point, REJECTED as blocking): the late media=playing gate cannot distinguish native loop from the ended->tryPlay() belt restarting the video. REJECTED because the acceptance is 'a looping video', not 'loops via the native attribute specifically'. The ended belt is intentional (Grok: belt in case native loop stalls); either mechanism yields a continuously looping video. media=playing past the clip duration proves continuous playback (looping); smoke separately asserts the literal loop attribute is present. Isolating the native attribute is not the acceptance and needs currentTime telemetry (deliberately omitted, no message handler). VERIFIED: VIDEO-CHECK PASS exit 0 on both displays (2 distinct wins == N; 7.5s late sample > ffprobe clip duration 6.0s; early t<=2.5 media=playing AND late t>6 media=playing); F61 video frame rendered edge-to-edge via -l; smoke green with shape guards. The looping video wallpaper starts on its own and fills the window. Webspike retirement deferred.

title: WebWallpaperView: transparent WKWebView with local file access
description: WKWebView configured transparent (no drawn background) with loadFileURL allowingReadAccessTo the web dir. Fills the window.
design: DECISION (Anoop): the public WKWebView transparency path is opaque on macOS 26; do NOT use the private drawsBackground KVC; accept an opaque base with a BLACK CSS fallback (the full-bleed video in ow-94b.2 covers it); true transparency deferred to ow-aqx.4. WebWallpaperView is a WKWebView SUBCLASS (WKNavigationDelegate) used directly as the WallpaperWindow content view (fills via being the contentView). init(frame:webDirectory:screenName:): config mediaTypesRequiringUserActionForPlayback=[]; super.init(frame:configuration:); underPageBackgroundColor=.clear (kept, harmless, future-relevant); navigationDelegate=self. Do NOT set/override isOpaque (opaque base is intended). Before load: FileManager.fileExists check + log dir/index_exists. loadFileURL(dir/index.html, allowingReadAccessTo: dir) (read root is the DIR). Navigation diagnostics: loaded=ok (didFinish, with screen+win), loaded=fail (didFail/didFailProvisional, with url+error), terminated (webContentProcessDidTerminate). NO telemetry/heartbeat/message-handler/z-order/KVC/allowsInlineMediaPlayback. AppDelegate resolves the web dir via #filePath ONLY (no WALLPAPER_WEB_DIR; that is ow-94b.3), stays WebKit-free (references WebWallpaperView type, not WKWebView), creates one per NSScreen.screens as the WallpaperWindow contentView (replacing the removed PlaceholderWallpaperView). Stub web/index.html: ONE file, inline CSS, full-bleed BLACK fallback (html,body{background:#000}) + color-scheme:only light + a centered marker label; 'replace entirely in ow-94b.2'. The env-gated webspike (WebSpikeWindow/web/webspike/webspike-check/OW_WEBSPIKE) is KEPT as the A/B until ow-94b.2 retires it. smoke allows WKWebView in WebWallpaperView.swift AND WebSpikeWindow.swift.
notes: Done (per the opaque-base decision). WebWallpaperView is a WKWebView subclass used directly as the WallpaperWindow content view: mediaTypesRequiringUserActionForPlayback=[], underPageBackgroundColor=.clear (public only, no drawsBackground KVC), loadFileURL(index.html, allowingReadAccessTo: dir). Loads a black-fallback stub (ow-94b.2 adds the real video page). AppDelegate resolves the web dir via #filePath (WALLPAPER_WEB_DIR + Bundle.module are ow-94b.3) and stays WebKit-free. Verified on 2 displays: index_exists=true, 2 distinct-win loaded=ok with frame>100x100, windows behind icons (zorder_ok=true) with click-through/all-Spaces flags; black fallback renders edge-to-edge (confirmed via screencapture -l). FINDING: public WKWebView transparency is opaque on macOS 26; base is opaque + black fallback (full-bleed video covers it); true transparency deferred to ow-aqx.4. Webspike kept env-gated as the A/B until ow-94b.2. 4 cold Codex passes to zero BLOCKING.
close_reason: WebWallpaperView (WKWebView subclass) fills each WallpaperWindow and loads a local page via loadFileURL, verified on two displays (index_exists, loaded=ok, frame>100x100, behind icons). Opaque base + black fallback per decision (true transparency deferred to ow-aqx.4). Default run now shows the web layer. Unblocks ow-94b.2 (real video page) and ow-94b.3 (asset resolution).

title: WallpaperWindow: desktop-layer, borderless, click-through
description: Borderless NSWindow at desktop window level; collectionBehavior canJoinAllSpaces+stationary+ignoresCycle; ignoresMouseEvents; isOpaque=false, clear background, no shadow. Fills the main screen.
design: Production WallpaperWindow as 'final class WallpaperWindow: NSWindow', init(screen:contentView:), copying the validated web-spike factory body VERBATIM (borderless at construction; level=NSWindow.Level(rawValue: Int(CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopWindow))); ASSIGN collectionBehavior=[.canJoinAllSpaces,.stationary,.ignoresCycle] (not formUnion); ignoresMouseEvents=true; hidesOnDeactivate=false; hasShadow=false; isOpaque=false; backgroundColor=.clear; isReleasedWhenClosed=false; setFrame(screen.frame, display:false)). Override canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain -> false. ONE window PER NSScreen.screens (a loop, retained array in AppDelegate), NOT main-only (findings say one-per-screen; NSScreen.main can be nil; Phase 5 host has 2 displays); union/slice/hot-plug remain ow-blz.1. Placeholder content: a plain NSView subclass, isOpaque=true, draw(_:) fills bounds with a saturated color + a TEMPORARY 'ow-94b.1 adds web layer' label (no wantsLayer, no timers); ow-94b.1 swaps it for WebWallpaperView. After orderFrontRegardless, run the ported CGWindowList z-order check and emit 'ONLYWALLPAPERS_WINDOW level=<raw> win=<number> layer=<actual> zorder_ok=<bool>'. AppDelegate: add applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed -> false (doc for blz.1 rebuilds); remove OW_SPIKE branch entirely incl. the dual-set refusal; keep OW_WEBSPIKE. DELETE SpikeWindow.swift + scripts/spike-check.sh (superseded). smoke-run.sh: \bNSWindow\b word-boundary, exclude WallpaperWindow.swift + WebSpikeWindow.swift; after liveness require exactly N ONLYWALLPAPERS_WINDOW lines each with level=-2147483623 AND zorder_ok=true; keep env -u OW_SPIKE -u OW_WEBSPIKE. Keep WebSpikeWindow/webspike for ow-94b.1.
acceptance_criteria: Window sits behind icons, passes clicks through, is present on every Space.
notes: Done. Production WallpaperWindow (final NSWindow subclass, borderless desktop-layer, content-agnostic, canBecomeKey/canBecomeMain false), one per NSScreen.screens by the default run, with a temporary opaque teal placeholder (ow-94b.1 swaps in WebWallpaperView). Verified on the 2-display host: placeholder renders (confirmed via screencapture -l of the window backing store); behind-icons proven by live CGWindowList zorder_ok=true and layer=-2147483623 (below icon level -2147483603) on both displays; click-through (ignoresMouseEvents) and all-Spaces (canJoinAllSpaces+stationary+ignoresCycle) asserted at runtime by smoke-run.sh (mouse/cb_* flags) and inherited from the byte-identical validated spike config. ow-mbw.1 spike (SpikeWindow.swift, spike-check.sh, OW_SPIKE) removed; WebSpike kept for ow-94b.1. applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed -> false for blz.1 window rebuilds. 3 cold Codex passes to zero BLOCKING. Fuller behavioral run-check remains ow-mbw.4. ow-local docs updated.
close_reason: Production WallpaperWindow shipped: borderless desktop-layer NSWindow subclass, one per screen by the default run, behind icons (live zorder_ok=true both displays), click-through + all-Spaces (flags asserted in smoke + byte-identical to the validated spike config), canBecomeKey/Main false, placeholder renders (verified). ow-mbw.1 spike retired. Seeds ow-94b.1 (content) and ow-blz.1 (geometry).

title: SwiftPM package skeleton + app lifecycle
description: Package.swift (executable), main.swift, AppDelegate. NSApplication with .accessory activation policy (no Dock icon, no Info.plist). App launches and stays running.
design: Target: single executableTarget OnlyWallpapers at Sources/OnlyWallpapers (main.swift + AppDelegate.swift). Package.swift: swift-tools-version 6.2, platforms [.macOS(.v14)], swiftSettings [.defaultIsolation(MainActor.self)]. No Info.plist, no resources, no second target (if empty web/ trips a SwiftPM unhandled-files warning, exclude web for now; ow-94b.3 converts it to a Bundle.module resource). main.swift: plain top-level code (NSApplication.shared, retain delegate as top-level let, assign, app.run()); no @MainActor annotation and no withExtendedLifetime (defaultIsolation covers actor isolation, top-level let covers lifetime). AppDelegate: final NSObject + NSApplicationDelegate; set NSApp.setActivationPolicy(.accessory) in applicationWillFinishLaunching (canonical pre-window hook, avoids Dock flicker) and precondition its Bool return; emit a stdout ready line including the runtime policy. scripts/smoke-run.sh is the behavioral quality gate.
acceptance_criteria: swift build --product OnlyWallpapers -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors is clean. App launches, sets and KEEPS .accessory policy verified at runtime (not inferred from absence of a Dock icon), stays alive, and exits cleanly on SIGINT. Quality gate is scripts/smoke-run.sh which: builds with warnings-as-errors, execs the built binary (not swift run) and tracks its PID, polls for the ready line with policy=accessory and kill -0, requires the PID to stay alive a further ~2s, verifies kill -INT makes it exit within ~1s, and scope-greps sources to fail if NSWindow/WKWebView/didChangeScreenParametersNotification/Info.plist appear. This change intentionally adds NO XCTest/test target: a unit test around NSApplication.run() would block or be tautological, so the smoke script is the test.
notes: Phase 1 complete (Opus plan + blind Codex co-scope + Grok red-team). All 12 Grok objections ACCEPTED. Key corrections vs initial draft: (1) one legal Swift 6 entry recipe via tools 6.2 + defaultIsolation(MainActor.self), not @MainActor on top-level code; (2) unbundled no-plist default is .prohibited (windows illegal), so smoke MUST assert runtime .accessory, not just 'no Dock icon'; (3) set policy in willFinishLaunching, check the Bool; (4) exec the built binary not swift run, INT-then-KILL trap. Scope boundary with ow-mbw.4: mbw.2 owns process-lives only; mbw.4 owns window-config/collectionBehavior assertions. Do NOT add applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed here (default is already false; if ever added it must return false, a mbw.3 decision). ow-local doc updates are Opus-owned, done after Phase 5, not by Sonnet. Full plan: /tmp/ow-consensus-plan.md.
close_reason: Skeleton built, reviewed (3 Codex passes to zero BLOCKING), and verified live: builds clean under warnings-as-errors, runs as .accessory (OS reports UIElement), stays alive, exits cleanly on SIGINT.

title: Spike: validate desktop-layer window renders continuously on Tahoe
description: Timeboxed: confirm a borderless NSWindow at CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopWindow) sits behind icons, stays click-through, joins all Spaces, and keeps animating (not frozen like built-in dynamic wallpapers) on macOS 26. De-risks the whole project.
design: Env-gated (OW_SPIKE=1) desktop-layer spike, default run unchanged. NEW Sources/OnlyWallpapers/SpikeWindow.swift (marked SPIKE, kept in-tree until ow-mbw.3 copies the factory). Window factory exact order: NSWindow(contentRect: screen.frame, styleMask: [.borderless], backing: .buffered, defer: false) created borderless (never mutate styleMask, Tahoe 26.3 regression); level = NSWindow.Level(rawValue: Int(CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopWindow))) (Int() for sign extension); collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces,.stationary,.ignoresCycle]; ignoresMouseEvents=true; hidesOnDeactivate=false; hasShadow=false; isOpaque=true + opaque magenta fill (behind-icons must be visual, not click-through); isReleasedWhenClosed=false; setFrame(display:false); retain in AppDelegate; orderFrontRegardless (not makeKeyAndOrderFront). One window per NSScreen.screens, print each localizedName. Probe: CADisplayLink via NSView.displayLink added to RunLoop .common (NOT Timer.scheduledTimer which is .default only); AppKit drawRect probe (drawCount) + CA probe (CALayer+CABasicAnimation, sample presentation); huge readable on-screen counter. Heartbeat once/sec via FileHandle.standardOutput.write (NOT print, which block-buffers): screen, driver, draws, ca, occlusionState, isVisible, level, zorder_ok. Behind-icons proof via CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo: self kCGWindowLayer strictly below Finder desktop-icon window (record FINDING, do not abort). App Nap: AppDelegate holds ProcessInfo.beginActivity(.userInitiatedAllowingIdleSystemSleep). AppDelegate emits READY line before building spike windows.
acceptance_criteria: A manual run shows a visibly animating window behind desktop icons that ignores clicks and appears on all Spaces.
notes: PHASE 5 COMPLETE (manual, Anoop, 2 displays / 2 Spaces). Behind-icons PASS (icons drag fine and stay on top; pixel-proven on display 1 where the on-screen counter advanced 366->424 across two real screenshots), click-through PASS, all-Spaces PASS (both Spaces), continuous animation PASS (pixel diff + CoreAnimation presentation at real-time rate, even under reported occlusion). Rendered-output acceptance was verified by Opus inspecting the real screenshots and by the user viewing live; the spike-check.sh pixel diff is a COARSE HINT only (the authoritative gate is that manual/visual inspection, which is the required gate per the task's 'manual run shows' acceptance). Per-screen windows show a duplicated look (NOT spanned); the spanned union canvas is Epic C (ow-blz). EDGE FINDING filed as ow-aad.4: dragging a desktop widget briefly reveals the real system wallpaper, then our content returns on drop. VERDICT: desktop-layer premise de-risked for AppKit+CoreAnimation; WKWebView video path is ow-94b.5. Reviewed over 4 cold Codex passes; final remaining Codex BLOCKING (automated pixel gate cannot guarantee a non-frozen surface) is resolved via the explicit manual-inspection gate, which Codex offered as an acceptable alternative.
close_reason: Spike done and verified: borderless desktop-layer NSWindow renders continuously behind icons on Tahoe (does not freeze, even under reported occlusion), click-through, all Spaces, on two displays. Proven by pixel screenshots + real-time CoreAnimation probe + manual Phase 5. Config and oracle lessons recorded in ow-local; WKWebView video de-risk is ow-94b.5; widget-drag reveal is ow-aad.4.

title: Epic C: Multi-monitor spanning
description: One window per screen, each showing its slice of a single logical canvas (union of all NSScreen frames), respecting the Displays arrangement. Rebuilds on display hot-plug/arrangement change. See DEC-002.

title: Epic B: Web render layer (single screen)
description: A transparent WKWebView in the window renders a looping base video from a local HTML/CSS/JS page. Establishes the render layer that all visual control builds on. See DEC-001.

title: Epic A: Native shell foundation
description: A running AppKit background utility (.accessory, no Dock icon) that pins one borderless, click-through, desktop-level window on the main screen. Proves the always-animated desktop-layer trick on macOS 26 (Tahoe). No private APIs.

title: True WKWebView desktop-through transparency on macOS 26 (public path is opaque)
description: Finding from ow-94b.1: on macOS 26 the public WKWebView transparency path (underPageBackgroundColor=.clear + transparent html/body CSS) does NOT make the base transparent; it renders opaque (an screencapture -l of the window interior comes back opaque, not the black that a truly transparent buffer yields). The de-facto macOS fix is the semi-private KVC setValue(false, forKey: 'drawsBackground'), which the project chose to avoid. For now WebWallpaperView uses an opaque base with a black CSS fallback, and the full-bleed video covers it, so the wallpaper itself is unaffected. This task is only needed when an Epic D overlay/blend effect actually needs the real desktop to show THROUGH the web layer. Then decide: accept the drawsBackground KVC (document the private-API risk), or find a public macOS 26 approach (overriding isOpaque, a transparent CALayer host, an alternate view). Verify with a hollow-interior page: screencapture -D of an uncovered display must show the real desktop through the interior.
acceptance_criteria: Either a public macOS 26 approach yields a genuinely transparent WKWebView base (desktop visible through a hollow page region in a -D display capture), or the drawsBackground KVC is adopted with the private-API risk documented and a fallback if it breaks.

title: Multi-display slice sync + pause/resume when displays are on different Spaces
description: Surfaced during the ow-94b.5 web-video de-risk (observed by Anoop on macOS 26.5.2). The spanned canvas (DEC-002) is one screen-sized WKWebView window PER display, each showing a slice of one oversized stage, with an independent video decode per screen (see known-limitations). Observed per-window behavior: a display whose desktop Space is visible keeps animating; a display taken into a full-screen app Space has its wallpaper slice PAUSED (occlusion/Space culling) and RESUMES when returning to the desktop Space (not frozen). OPEN QUESTIONS for the spanned design: (1) When one display is in a full-screen Space while the other stays on the desktop, does the still-visible slice keep animating (expected yes) and does the hidden slice pause independently (expected yes)? (2) CRITICAL: when the paused slice resumes, is it FRAME-SYNCED with the other slice, or does it drift, breaking the continuous-across-the-bezel image? Investigate a shared playback clock / periodic resync (e.g. seek both <video> elements to a common wall-clock-derived time) so slices stay aligned across pause/resume and across independent decodes. Reuse the ow-94b.5 telemetry (currentTime per window) to measure drift.
acceptance_criteria: The spanned wallpaper keeps a single continuous image across displays, and slices stay frame-aligned (within tolerance) after one display pauses/resumes due to Spaces, verified by comparing per-window currentTime.

title: Sample bg.mp4 sourcing + docs

title: Window-config assertions + run check
description: Lightweight tests/assertions for the window level and collection behavior flags, plus a documented manual run check.

title: Epic E: Lifecycle and robustness
description: Survive the real world: Spaces, lock/unlock, sleep/wake, Stage Manager, and optional launch-at-login.

title: Epic D: Live control (the fun)
description: The creative layer: CSS filters, time-of-day moods, overlays, and minimal config. All editable in the web layer without recompiling Swift.

title: Transient real-wallpaper reveals during system transitions (widget drag, Space switch)
description: Our desktop-layer window is briefly replaced by the REAL system wallpaper during some system-driven transitions, then our content returns. Two observed instances on macOS 26.5.2 (ow-mbw.1 spike): (1) WIDGET DRAG: while dragging a desktop widget (clock, calendar), the real wallpaper (dimmed) shows in place of our window for the drag duration, returning on drop. (2) FULL-SCREEN TO DESKTOP SPACE SWITCH: navigating (cmd+arrow / swipe) from a full-screen app Space back to the desktop Space, the old/real wallpaper flashes for about a second during the slide animation before our window appears. Same class: the compositor shows the true desktop during the transition and our desktop-level window paints a beat late. Likely related to Mission Control / Space-transition surface snapshotting. Investigate whether either is preventable (window level/flags, reacting to transition notifications); may be inherent system behavior. Belongs with Spaces/lifecycle work (see ow-aad.1). Low priority.
design: Do NOT assume this is unfixable: research what macOS actually does during widget drag (widget-edit mode compositing, whether our desktop-level window can stay visible, any notifications for enter/exit widget-edit, window level/flags options). Candidate fallbacks if the reveal cannot be fully prevented: (1) PREFERRED: on drag/widget-edit start, grab a freeze-frame (thumbnail of the current rendered frame) and show it so the swap looks seamless, restoring live render on drag end; needs a way to detect widget-edit start quickly. (2) LOWER: set the user's actual system wallpaper to solid black so that whatever the OS reveals during widget drag is just black (not an unrelated photo), which looks intentional rather than jarring. Priority stays P3: user rarely drags widgets once placed.

notes: User guidance (Anoop): dig deeper and research, do not assume can/cannot be done. Low priority because widgets are rarely dragged once set.

title: smoke-run policy check relies on app self-report, not an independent query
description: NON-BLOCKING finding from the ow-mbw.2 Phase 3 review. scripts/smoke-run.sh asserts the activation policy from the app's own stdout ready line (ONLYWALLPAPERS_READY policy=accessory). A future hardcoded or drifted ready line could evade it. The static guard (setActivationPolicy called exactly once and is .accessory) plus the Bool precondition reduce the risk, but the runtime assertion is not independent. Options: query the OS classification during the liveness window (e.g. lsappinfo info -only ApplicationType -app <pid> should report UIElement for .accessory), which Phase 5 of ow-mbw.2 did manually. Fold that into the smoke script, or into ow-mbw.4 (window-config assertions + run check).
acceptance_criteria: smoke-run (or ow-mbw.4) verifies the runtime activation policy via an OS-level query independent of the app's own stdout.
